title: Chicken and Mushroom Pie
subtitle: Poached chicken in a creamy mushroom sauce under a puff pastry lid
excerpt: Chicken and mushroom pie is a white-sauce filling of poached chicken and sautéed mushrooms under a puff pastry lid. The sauce is built from the poaching stock so nothing is wasted, and the result is a deeply comforting, crowd-pleasing pie that works on a weeknight or a Sunday.
sourceNotes: Classic British white-sauce pie tradition. Adapted from general British home-cooking methods. Filling structure follows the cream-sauce pie form documented in 20th-century British home cookery guides.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the unbaked assembled pie for up to 2 months. Bake from frozen at 180°C for 50 to 55 minutes, covering lightly with foil if the pastry colours before the filling heats through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Cool completely before assembling.

content.text: Chicken and mushroom pie is poached chicken thighs and sautéed mushrooms in a cream sauce, topped with puff pastry. The sauce uses the poaching stock as its base, which keeps the filling from tasting flat. It is one of the most useful pies to know: mild, adaptable, and easy to make from what is in the fridge.

Put the chicken thighs in a saucepan, cover with cold water, and bring to a very gentle simmer. Skim off any foam, then cook for 18 to 20 minutes until just cooked through. Lift out the chicken and reserve the cooking liquid: strain and measure out 400 ml. When cool enough to handle, tear the chicken into large shreds.

Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the leek and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the mushrooms and cook for another 4 to 5 minutes until they have released their moisture and the pan is nearly dry.

Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually pour in the reserved chicken stock, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Once smooth, stir in the double cream. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Fold in the shredded chicken and tarragon if using. Taste and season. Tip into a pie dish and leave to cool completely.

Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Lay the puff pastry over the cooled filling, pressing the edge onto the rim of the dish. Trim the overhang and crimp or press with a fork. Cut two small vents in the top, brush with beaten egg, and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is deep gold and well risen.

items.symptom: Sauce too thin inside the finished pie
items.cause: Sauce was not reduced enough before assembly, or cream proportion was too high
items.fix: Simmer the sauce until it coats the back of a spoon thickly: it will thin slightly when hot inside the pie. A tablespoon less cream helps next time.

items.cause: Pastry was laid over a warm filling, softening the butter layers before baking
items.fix: Cool the filling fully before applying the pastry. You can also rest the assembled pie in the fridge for 20 minutes before baking.

items.cause: The poaching water was not salted and the sauce was under-seasoned
items.fix: Season the poaching water with a pinch of salt. Taste the sauce before assembly: it should be well seasoned at room temperature; it will taste less salty hot.

items.cause: Too much sauce evaporated during baking through a large vent
items.fix: Cut two small slits rather than a large hole. The sauce only needs a narrow vent to release steam.

content.text: Chicken and mushroom pie is the milder, more approachable sibling of the classic British meat pie. It became a supermarket freezer staple from the 1970s onwards, which somewhat overshadowed the homemade version: but the gap between the two is significant. A pie made with good stock and real cream has nothing in common with its frozen counterpart. It is one of the cleanest ways to use a batch of poached chicken.
